procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy for gallbladder torsion (gangrenous, acalculous gallbladder presenting as acute cholecystitis)
phase: decompression of the distended gallbladder (after derotation, before the cholecystectomy)
sources: video legend (Commons description = Additional file 1 legend of Boer et al., J Med Case Reports 2011, 5:588)
article full text PMC3259112: Case presentation, Discussion, Figure 2-4 legends
notes: Control clip (same window as v1 shot A). phase_time_s is the pipeline's shot window (cuts at 23.5 and 33.5 s); the legend gives 24-33 s for decompression. Excluded inputs: the SOURCE.md 'Shots:' line (which instrument touches what) is a human observation of the frames and was not used, so anything v1 modelled from the frames (instrument types in this shot, peritoneal strands / membrane) is NOT in this spec and must come from vision. Extra keys: instruments[].id, organs[].sam_prompt_alt, background[].source.

patient.condition: gallbladder torsion: two-fold twist around the cystic duct, strongly hydropic and fully necrotic (gangrenous) gallbladder without stones, gangrene extending into cystic duct and artery; clinically acute cholecystitis. Prior abdominal surgery decades ago (rectopexy, retropubic bladder suspension, hysterectomy; median laparotomy scar).

organs.name: gallbladder
organs.pathology: strongly hydropic (distended with fluid), gangrenous wall over the whole organ, wall 7 mm on admission ultrasound, no stones; free-floating on its pedicle; twist presumably undone in the previous phase
organs.expected_motion: loses volume (deflates) as its contents are drawn off; wall becomes slack and folds; little whole-organ rotation expected (derotation is the previous phase); local deformation at grasp and puncture points
organs.notes: Volume is NOT conserved in this clip once the lumen is opened. Contents not described (no stones; necrotic gallbladder fluid may be dark or bloody).

organs.name: cystic duct
organs.pathology: gangrene extends into the duct; was the torsion axis
organs.expected_motion: follows the gallbladder neck; anchored at the common hepatic/bile duct
organs.notes: Visibility in this window not stated.

organs.name: cystic artery
organs.expected_motion: follows the gallbladder neck; anchored at the hepatic artery
organs.notes: May be indistinguishable from the duct in the image.

organs.name: liver
organs.expected_motion: not manipulated according to the text; respiratory motion only
organs.notes: The gallbladder does not lie in the liver bed (not embedded).

connections.evidence: The gallbladder hung from the cystic duct and artery instead of lying in the liver (article, Case presentation).
Same sentence (article, Case presentation); Figure 4 legend: rotated around duct and artery.
Not embedded in the liver (article, Case presentation) = floating gallbladder. Do NOT attach it to the liver.
Together they form the pedicle (article); after derotation (legend 0-23 s) they are presumably no longer wound around each other.
Normal biliary anatomy; fixed anchor of the pedicle. Not described for this window.

instruments.evidence: Legend: decompression 24-33 s. Neither legend nor article names the device (could be an aspiration needle, a trocar or a suction cannula).
Not stated for this window. Graspers are standard in laparoscopic cholecystectomy and were needed for the derotation just before; 5 mm is a typical default.

actions.evidence: Legend: decompression 24-33 s, after derotation; Discussion: decompression and detorsion are the goals of laparoscopy in torsion.
actions.confidence: high for verb/target/time; low for the instrument type

openings.site: not stated (fundus is the usual site; low confidence)
openings.evidence: Decompressing a distended, closed gallbladder requires opening its lumen; legend places decompression at 24-33 s. Method and site are not described.
openings.notes: instrument is left null on purpose: the vision/instrument step must name the one tracked tool that enters the lumen; only that tool gets the opening. Puncture must be cut into the mesh at the observed entry point.

openings.evidence: Clipping/division belongs to the cholecystectomy phase (legend 34-42 s).

camera.scope: laparoscope; diameter and angle not stated (10 mm, 0 or 30 degree is typical; low confidence)
camera.notes: Text gives no port positions or patient position. Video 640x480, picture rows 59-419 (data prep).

background.name: gallbladder contents (spilled/aspirated fluid)
background.source: inferred from text: decompression of a strongly hydropic gallbladder releases fluid; appearance not described

background.name: peri-gallbladder fat
background.source: text: CT fatty infiltration around the gallbladder (article, Figure 2 legend)

background.name: free fluid
background.source: text: CT/ultrasound fluid above/below the liver and around the gallbladder (article); presence at laparoscopy not stated

physiology: respiration: ventilation moves the liver and hilum through the diaphragm and is transmitted to the gallbladder via its pedicle (anatomy, not in text; small, periodic)
deflation: the gallbladder volume falls as contents leave; this is caused by the instrument, not physiology, but it is the main non-rigid change to model
uncertain: How decompression is done (needle aspiration, trocar, suction cannula, incision) and with which instrument; where the wall is entered and when inside 23.5-33.5 s.
Which other instruments are in view and what they touch (holding the gallbladder, retracting tissue); v1's 'probe on peritoneal strands' is a frame observation, not text, and is not encoded here.
Whether peritoneal strands, adhesions or other membranes attach to the gallbladder (text: only the duct/artery pedicle; prior laparotomies make adhesions possible).
How much volume is removed in this window and whether contents spill into the field.
Whether the derotation was complete by 23.5 s (pedicle untwisted) or continues.
Visibility of duct, artery and liver; laparoscope and shaft diameters (scale).
